Document: Practice Direction 26 – Case management – preliminary stage: allocation, reallocation, assignment and reassignment
Part 2 of 2
==================================================
[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (1) Where the court is to decide whether to allocate to the fast track a claim for which the normal track is the fast track, it will allocate the claim to the fast track unless it believes that it cannot be dealt with justly on that track. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (2) The court will, in particular, take into account the limits likely to be placed on disclosure, the extent to which expert evidence may be necessary and whether the trial is likely to last more than a day. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (3)

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (a)  when it is considering the likely length of the trial the court will regard a day as being a period of 5 hours, and will consider whether that is likely to be sufficient time for the case to be heard;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (b)  the court will also take into account the case management directions (including the fixing of a trial timetable) that are likely to be given and the court’s powers to control evidence and to limit cross-examination;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (c)  subject to paragraph (e), the possibility that a trial might last longer than one day is not necessarily a conclusive reason for the court to allocate or to re-allocate a claim to the intermediate track or the multi-track;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (d)  a claim may be allocated to the fast track or ordered to remain on that track although there is to be a split trial;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (e)  where the case involves a counterclaim or additional claim that will be tried with the claim and as a result the trial will last more than a day, the court may not allocate it to the fast track. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (4) Directions for the case management of claims which have been allocated to the fast track will be given at the allocation stage or at the listing stage (in either case with or without a hearing) or at both or and if necessary at other times. The trial judge may, at or before the trial, give directions for its conduct. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 16.] (5) Practice Direction 28contains further provisions and contains standard directions which the court may give. ## The intermediate track – allocation and case management

## 17. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 17.] (1)Part 26 and, in particular, rules26.9(7) to (11), 26.12 and 26.13 make provision regarding the allocation of claims to the intermediate track. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 17.] (2) Part 28 and Practice Direction 28 make provision regarding the case management of claims allocated to the intermediate track. ## The multi-track – venue for allocation and case management

## 18. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (1) Sub-paragraphs (2) to (13) do not apply to—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (a)  a claim for possession of land in the County Court or a demotion claim whether in the alternative to a possession claim or under Part 65;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (b)  a Renting Homes possession claim as defined by rule 55.30 in the County Court or a prohibited conduct standard contract order claim as defined by rule 65.11 whether in the alternative to a Renting Homes possession claim or under Part 65; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (c)  any claim which is being dealt with at the Royal Courts of Justice. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (2) The case management of a claim which is allocated to the multi-track will normally be dealt with at a Civil Trial Centre. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (3) In the case of a claim to which any of Parts 49 or 58 to 62 apply, case management must be dealt with at a Civil Trial Centre. Sub-paragraphs (5) to (11) do not apply to such a claim. The claim will be allocated to the multi-track irrespective of its value, and must be transferred to a Civil Trial Centre for allocation and case management if not already there. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (4) Where a claim is issued in or automatically transferred to a Civil Trial Centre it will be allocated and managed at that court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (5) The following sub-paragraphs apply to a claim which is issued in or automatically transferred to a court which is not a Civil Trial Centre. Such a court is referred to as a ‘feeder court’. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (6) Where a judge sitting at a feeder court decides, on the basis of the directions questionnaires and any other documents filed by the parties, that the claim should be dealt with on the multi-track they will normally make an order—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (a)  allocating the claim to that track;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (b)  giving case management directions; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (c)  transferring the claim to a Civil Trial Centre. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (7) If the judge decides that an allocation hearing, or some pre-allocation hearing is to take place (for example to strike out a statement of case under Part 3 of the Rules) that hearing will take place at the feeder court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (8) If, before allocation, a hearing takes place at a feeder court and in exercising their powers under paragraph 5.(a) above the judge allocates the claim to the multi-track, they will also normally make an order transferring the claim to a Civil Trial Centre. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (9) A judge sitting at a feeder court may, rather than making an allocation order himself, transfer the claim to a Civil Trial Centre for the decision about allocation to be taken there. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (10) When, following an order for transfer, the file is received at the Civil Trial Centre, a judge sitting at that Centre will consider it and give any further directions that appear necessary or desirable. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (11) Where there is reason to believe that more than one case management conference may be needed and the parties or their legal advisers are located inconveniently far from the Civil Trial Centre, a judge sitting at a feeder court may, with the agreement of the Designated Civil Judge and notwithstanding the allocation of the case to the multi-track, decide that in the particular circumstances of the case it should not be transferred to a Civil Trial Centre, but should be case managed for the time being at the feeder court. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (12) A Designated Civil Judge may at any time make an order transferring a claim from a feeder court to a Civil Trial Centre and may do so irrespective of the track, if any, to which it has been allocated. They may also permit a feeder court to keep for trial a claim or (subject to review from time to time) a category of claims. Any such permission should take into account the ability of the feeder court in relation to the Civil Trial Centre to provide suitable and effective trial within an appropriate trial period. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (13) No order will be made by a feeder court fixing a date for a hearing at a Civil Trial Centre unless that date has been given or confirmed by a judge or listing officer of that Centre. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 18.] (14)Part 29 of the Rules and Practice Direction 29 set out the procedure to be adopted regarding case management. ## Money claims sent to the County Court at Central London

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > Money claims sent to the County Court at Central London] 19. The County Court hearing centres referred to in rule 26.3(6)(c) are Barnet, Brentford, Bromley, Central London, Clerkenwell and Shoreditch, Croydon, Edmonton, Kingston-on-Thames, Lambeth, Mayors and City of London, Romford, Wandsworth, Willesden, and Uxbridge. ## Determining the amount to be paid under a judgment or order

## 20. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (1) In paragraphs 21 to 24—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (a)  a ‘relevant order’ means a judgment or order of the court which requires the amount of money to be paid by one party to another to be decided by the court; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (b)  a ‘disposal hearing’ means a hearing in accordance with paragraph 23. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (2) A relevant order may have been obtained—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (a)  by a judgment in default under Part 12;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (b)  by a judgment on an admission under Part 14;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (c)  on the striking out of a statement of case under Part 3;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (d)  on a summary judgment application under Part 24;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (e)  on the determination of a preliminary issue or on a trial as to liability; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (f) at trial. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 20.] (3) A relevant order includes any order for the amount of a debt, damages or interest to be decided by the court (including an order for the taking of an account or the making of an inquiry as to any sum due, and any similar order), but does not include an order for the assessment of costs. ## Directions on making a relevant order

## 21. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 21.] (1) When the court makes a relevant order it will give directions, which may include—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 21.] (a)  listing the claim for a disposal hearing;

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 21.] (b)  allocating or re-allocating the claim (but see paragraph 22);

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 21.] (c)  directing the parties to file directions questionnaires by a specified date; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 21.] (d)  staying the claim while the parties try to settle the case by alternative dispute resolution or other means. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 21.] (2) Directions may specify the level or type of judge before whom a hearing or a further hearing will take place and the nature and purpose of that hearing. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 21.] (3) Where the parties apply for a relevant order by consent, they should if possible file with their draft consent order agreed directions for the court’s approval. ## Allocation on making a relevant order

## 22. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 22.] (1) If, when the court makes a relevant order—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 22.] (a)  the claim has not previously been allocated to a track; and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 22.] (b)  the financial value of the claim (determined in accordance with Part 26) is such that the claim would, if defended be allocated to the small claims track,

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 22.] the court will normally allocate it to that track. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 22.] (2) Where paragraph (1)(b) does not apply, the court will not normally allocate the claim to a track (other than the small claims track) unless—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 22.] (a)  the amount payable appears to be genuinely disputed on substantial grounds; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 22.] (b)  the dispute is not suitable to be dealt with at a disposal hearing. ## Disposal hearings

## 23. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (1) A disposal hearing is a hearing—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (a)  which will not normally last longer than 30 minutes, and

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (b)  at which the court will not normally hear oral evidence. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (2) At a disposal hearing the court may—

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (a)  decide the amount payable under or in consequence of the relevant order and give judgment for that amount; or

[PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (b)  give directions as to the future conduct of the proceedings. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (3) If the claim has been allocated to the small claims track, or the court decides at the disposal hearing to allocate it to that track, the court may treat the disposal hearing as a final hearing in accordance with Part 27. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (4) Rule 32.6 applies to evidence at a disposal hearing unless the court directs otherwise. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 23.] (5) Except where the claim has been allocated to the small claims track, the court will not exercise its power under sub-paragraph (2)(a) unless any written evidence on which the claimant relies has been served on the defendant at least 3 days before the disposal hearing. ## Jurisdiction of Masters and District Judges

## 24. [PRACTICE DIRECTION 26 – CASE MANAGEMENT – PRELIMINARY STAGE: ALLOCATION, REALLOCATION, ASSIGNMENT AND REASSIGNMENT > 24.] Unless the court otherwise directs, a Master or a District Judge may decide the amount payable under a relevant order irrespective of the financial value of the claim and of the track to which the claim may have been allocated.”
